internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every time this root appears in the Quran it is the same one word-form, muhTiEin, describing unbelievers at a scene of summons or judgment. The safe, uncontested meaning is a body-and-attention 'strained forward and locked on,' under compulsion or dread. When the verse adds 'toward the caller' (54:8) or 'toward you' (70:36) it looks like straining/hurrying toward a target; but 14:43 has no target at all and shows a frozen, staring, craned posture. The root itself supplies the strained-fixed-attention part; the 'toward X' and the speed come from the surrounding words, not from the root.

Does NOT mean neck/head-raising (14:43 assigns that to the separate adjacent word مُقْنِعِى رُءُوسِهِمْ).
